items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: And the thing is when you go back and listen to those records by the Freddie Websters and Lester Youngs, they didn’t play a whole lot of choruses.

ctx.x: They couldn’t go on and on and on.

Well Max Roach was telling me that when the 78s were, that sometimes you would only get four bars. And even in playing in the bands. And that’s what spawned a lot of the jam sessions because guys were frustrated because they wanted to improvise and stretch out more. But sometimes in a band you might have one tune that was your feature for that night, and if you acted up with the band leader you might not even get to play it that night. So then you’d leave there a nervous wreck. “I didn’t get a chance to really do…
him then Prez kind of waltzed back again and said, “If you’ve got eyes, Prez, the slave is yours.” And that’s how he got hired with Lester Young.
